intro: Sofia rewards visitors with Roman ruins, grand churches and mountain views a short ride away. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro Line 4 links the airport to the centre in about 40 min.
Buses, trams and trolleybuses run 05:00-23:00, plus four night lines.
A single ticket costs about 1.60 лв; a day card about 4 лв.
Contactless bank cards and Apple/Google Pay work on gates and readers.
Taxis are yellow; use OK Supertrans or the Ridenow app.
The centre is walkable, but pavements are uneven and potholed.

nevsky.name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Sofia
nevsky.price_text: Free to enter the cathedral · crypt museum around BGN 6
nevsky.hours: Daily roughly 07:00–19:00 · check on the day
nevsky.tip: Go early morning for quiet photos of the gold domes, then visit the icon crypt museum below.

boyana.name: Boyana Church
boyana.price_text: ≈ BGN 10 entry · short timed visits only
boyana.hours: Check on the day · usually closed some weekdays
boyana.tip: Entry is in small timed groups, so arrive early and expect a short 10-minute visit inside.

stgeorge.name: Church of St George (Rotunda)
stgeorge.hours: Daily roughly 08:00–18:00 · check on the day
stgeorge.tip: It sits in a courtyard behind the Presidency, so look for the passage off the main square.

vitosha-blvd.name: Vitosha Boulevard
vitosha-blvd.tip: Walk it in the evening when it fills with locals, and look up for the Vitosha mountain at the far end.

shopska.name: Shopska Salad
shopska.hours: Served at most restaurants from lunch to late evening
shopska.tip: Order it as a starter with rakia; the grated white cheese on top is the point.

synagogue.name: Sofia Synagogue
synagogue.price_text: ≈ BGN 5 small entry fee · check on the day
synagogue.hours: Weekdays roughly 09:00–17:00 · closed Saturday and Jewish holidays
synagogue.tip: One of the largest Sephardic synagogues in Europe; men may be asked to cover their head.

central-market.name: Central Sofia Market Hall (Halite)
central-market.price_text: Free to enter · food priced per item
central-market.tip: Good for cheese, banitsa and local snacks; the upper floor has cheap eateries.

women-market.name: Zhenski Pazar (Women's Market)
women-market.price_text: Free to browse · pay per item
women-market.tip: Come early for produce and local cheese; keep valuables close in the crowds.

free-tour.name: Free walking tour of central Sofia
free-tour.hours: Usually daily around 10:00 and 18:00 · check on the day
free-tour.tip: Book online the day before and meet near the Palace of Justice; wear comfortable shoes.

vitoshka-view.name: Vitosha mountain viewpoint (Aleko area)
vitoshka-view.price_text: Free · cable car and transport cost extra
vitoshka-view.hours: Mountain always open · cable car check on the day
vitoshka-view.tip: Take a bus or taxi up to Aleko for city views and short walks; bring a jacket, it is cooler up there.

borisova.name: Borisova Gradina Park
borisova.tip: Big green park with paths and cafes; good for a relaxed afternoon walk away from traffic.

roman-ruins.name: Ancient Serdica ruins (metro underpass)
roman-ruins.tip: Roman street remains sit right inside the metro station; a quick free stop near the main sights.

ndk-view.name: NDK park and fountains
ndk-view.tip: Sit by the fountains at sunset; it is a popular local meeting spot with Vitosha views.

banitsa-breakfast.name: Banitsa and boza breakfast
banitsa-breakfast.price_text: ≈ BGN 3–7 for banitsa and a drink
banitsa-breakfast.hours: Bakeries usually open early to evening
banitsa-breakfast.tip: Try warm banitsa with a glass of boza or ayran; cheap and very local.

vitoshka-cafes.name: Cafe-hopping around Graf Ignatiev and Solunska
vitoshka-cafes.tip: Wander the side streets off Vitosha Blvd for small cafes and bars; prices are lower than the main street.

national-museum.name: National Museum of History
national-museum.hours: Usually daily roughly 09:30–18:00 · check on the day
national-museum.tip: It is far out in Boyana, so pair it with Boyana Church in one trip.

sveta-nedelya.name: Sveta Nedelya Church
sveta-nedelya.tip: Central church right by the main square; step in for the frescoes on a walking route.

rakia-bar.name: Evening rakia and meze bar
rakia-bar.tip: Order a small rakia with shopska salad or grilled meat; go slow, it is strong.

tram-ride.name: Tram ride through the city centre
tram-ride.tip: Buy and validate a ticket before boarding; a cheap way to see everyday Sofia.

book-market.name: Second-hand book stalls on Slaveykov Square
book-market.price_text: Free to browse · books priced per item
book-market.tip: Browse the open-air book market and the nearby cafes; a relaxed local corner.

stays.why: Walk to the cathedral, Roman ruins and the main sights. Best base for a first visit.
The main pedestrian street: cafés, shops and easy walking to everything central.
Quiet, leafy and local, with good metro and tram links to the centre.
Cheapest beds and lively student bars, but a metro or bus ride from the sights.

food: Try Bulgarian classics: shopska salad, banitsa pastry and grilled meats at a mehana (tavern).
Breakfast on the go: a warm banitsa with ayran (yogurt drink) from a bakery counter, cheap and filling.
Look for lunch menus (obedno menu) at local restaurants; they cost far less than dinner.
Vegetarians are well served: shopska salad, roasted peppers and sirene (white cheese) dishes are everywhere.
Tipping is modest, around 10%. Check the bill; some places add a service charge.
more_time: Day trip to Rila Monastery: a UNESCO site in the mountains, roughly 2 hours each way. Check bus times on the day.
Add Plovdiv, a historic old town about 2 hours by bus or train, for a night or a long day.
Hike Vitosha mountain: take the cable car or a bus up and walk back down in a half day.
